# CI integration and reproducible reporting

**Status:** experimental, read-only, supplied-file comparison. Reviewed 2026-10-10. The example inputs in repository CI are **synthetic XDR generated by unit-test helpers**, not real Stellar network/ETL evidence.

## Generate a local report

```bash
python -m pip install '.[source]'
ledgerverity reconcile \
  --source original-rpc.json \
  --candidate candidate-etl.jsonl \
  --scope candidate.scope.json \
  --format json --output report.json --summary-output report.md
```

- Exit `3` means the comparison ran and produced an **INCONCLUSIVE** or **REVIEW_REQUIRED** observational report. Treat it as an expected exit code, not as a chain error.
- Exit `2` means invalid input or unable to write output; fail the job and investigate.
- `--format markdown` can print/write a fixed-layout Markdown summary directly. `--summary-output` writes the same summary alongside JSON/text output.
- JSON preserves the earlier `schema_version: 1` fields and adds an explicitly versioned `report_contract: ledgerverity.reconciliation-report.v1` with `evidence_fingerprints`, `evidence_gates`, `review_guidance` and review-only classifications per displayed finding. See [report schema](REPORT_SCHEMA.md).
- A Markdown summary contains **only fixed labels, numeric values and SHA-256 digests**, not untrusted exporter/manifest free text. This prevents input data from injecting headings or external links into the GitHub Actions summary.
- A report destination cannot alias source, candidate or manifest input, including symlinks to them. Reports are written via replacement from temporary files in the output directory to avoid partially truncating prior reports.

## CI status evaluation: explicitly opt in to a review failure

```bash
# The reconcile CLI deliberately returns 3 for all valid comparisons.
set +e
ledgerverity reconcile --source original-rpc.json --candidate candidate-etl.jsonl \
  --scope candidate.scope.json --format json --output report.json \
  --summary-output report.md
rc=$?
set -e
test "$rc" -eq 3

# Validates report contract and that no false verification is claimed.
ledgerverity-ci-gate --report report.json

# Optional local policy: exit 1 on REVIEW_REQUIRED, not on INCONCLUSIVE.
ledgerverity-ci-gate --report report.json --fail-on-review

# GitHub Actions only (environment variable provided by GitHub):
cat report.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

The small `ledgerverity-ci-gate` tool rejects malformed/missing reports and forged assertions of verified consensus, network or full export coverage (exit 2). Without `--fail-on-review` it returns 0 for either valid observational status; with the option, `REVIEW_REQUIRED` returns 1. This is **your local CI policy**, never proof of a real Stellar ETL defect. A clean-looking `INCONCLUSIVE` report does not certify parity.

See the inert, copyable [workflow example](../examples/github-actions/reconcile.yml) (not a registered workflow). It requires the consuming repository to provision input data securely; LedgerVerity itself makes **no network calls**. Only upload report files if their manifest, transaction hashes and source references are permitted to be shared with GitHub Actions storage. Avoid uploading private inputs or RPC credentials.

## What our own repository CI verifies

The normal GitHub Actions matrix tests Python 3.10 and 3.12. It generates one synthetic `exact` fixture and one synthetic `source-only` fixture from SDK-serialized test XDR, then runs the **installed** CLI with JSON and Markdown outputs, validates both with the CI gate, and explicitly checks the opt-in review exit code. The job summary and version-suffixed 7-day artifacts are labeled synthetic. Both regressions and real-data trust limitations are visible.

Official GitHub references: [job summaries](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands#adding-a-job-summary), [artifact retention and input options](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/action.yml). The workflow does not create a real ETL-export fixture, independently attest ledger history, or submit a Drips/Wave application.
